findings: All eight complete CPU/NPU capture outputs retain their historical hashes. All sixty-three captured packet replies retain pixels and coverage. Instrumentation does not change the graph arithmetic or execution properties.

For both full-screen captures, the 8192-lane NPU pixel stage spends approximately 4.2 seconds per warm draw in infer calls; complete warm draws remain about seven seconds. Host input packing and copying are measurable but do not dominate these two full draws.

The mixed replay creates 120 Core objects and performs 117 model compile/load operations, all persistent-cache hits. Core construction totals 121.689 ms, compile_model calls 5484.876 ms, and cache directory/key configuration 2713.277 ms. These timings do not include every graph-building and model-loading step.

Low Core constructor time does not isolate lazy plugin initialization within later API calls. Shared-Core benefits are not established or ruled out by these counters. CompiledModel sharing remains disabled after the earlier device-loss experiment.

Host-side infer timers include runtime and submission overhead; they do not identify the NPU hardware engine or per-operation bottleneck. Official compiler profiling is a possible further diagnostic, not a result of this experiment.
No installed desktop trial or CPU build overlaps these serial replay measurements. The next cache-capacity candidate requires separate qualification and installed testing.
